questions.text: स्त्रियों (मानव मादा) में गर्भ उत्क्षेपण प्रतिवर्त (फीटल इजेक्शन रेफलेक्स) किस हॉर्मोन के स्रवण को उद्दीपित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Foetal ejection reflex in human female triggers the release of which hormone?

options.A: गर्भ की पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन

questions.solution: The foetal ejection reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary gland, which causes stronger uterine contractions leading to parturition.
questions.solution_hindi: गर्भ उत्क्षेपण प्रतिवर्त मातृ पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन के स्रवण को उद्दीपित करता है, जिससे गर्भाशय में तीव्र संकुचन होता है और प्रसव प्रक्रिया संपन्न होती है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पारितंत्र की प्रकार्यात्मक इकाई नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a functional unit of an ecosystem?
questions.solution: Stratification is the vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem, which is a structural feature, not a functional unit. Functional units include productivity, decomposition, energy flow, and nutrient cycling.
questions.solution_hindi: स्तरण (Stratification) एक पारितंत्र की संरचनात्मक विशेषता है जो विभिन्न स्तरों पर प्रजातियों के ऊर्ध्वाधर वितरण को दर्शाती है, यह प्रकार्यात्मक इकाई नहीं है।

questions.text:
कॉलम I में दी गई मदों का कॉलम II में दी गई मदों से मिलान कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
कॉलम I
a. प्रारंभक (प्राइमर)
b. निवेशी निष्क्रियता (इनसर्शनल इनऐक्टीवेशन)
c. बायोरिऐक्टर
d. अनुप्रवाह संसाधन

कॉलम II
i. ẞ-गैलेक्टोसाइडेज़
ii. उत्पादों का पृथक्करण तथा परिष्करण (शोधन)
iii. रासायनिक रूप से संश्लेषित ऑलिगोन्यूक्लियोटाइड्स
iv. सूक्ष्मजीवीय प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा विशिष्ट उत्पादों का वृहद् स्तर पर उत्पादन
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II and select the correct option:
Column I
a. Primers
b. Insertional inactivation
c. Bioreactor
d. Downstream processing

Column II
i. ẞ-galactosidase
ii. To separate and purify products
iii. Chemically synthesized oligonucleotides
iv. Large scale production of specific product of activity of microbes
questions.solution: Primers are chemically synthesized oligonucleotides used in PCR. Insertional inactivation is a technique used in recombinant DNA technology, often involving the beta-galactosidase gene. Bioreactors are vessels for large scale production of specific products using microbes. Downstream processing involves the separation and purification of products before they are marketed. Thus, option A correctly matches all terms.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रारंभक (प्राइमर) रासायनिक रूप से संश्लेषित ऑलिगोन्यूक्लियोटाइड्स होते हैं। निवेशी निष्क्रियता ẞ-गैलेक्टोसाइडेज़ जीन से संबंधित है। बायोरिऐक्टर सूक्ष्मजीवीय प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा विशिष्ट उत्पादों के वृहद् स्तर पर उत्पादन के लिए प्रयुक्त होते हैं और अनुप्रवाह संसाधन उत्पादों के पृथक्करण और शोधन से संबंधित है। अतः विकल्प (A) सही है।

questions.text: गोल्डन राइस एक उदीयमान पारजीनी फ़सल है। इसे जब खेतों में उगाने के लिए निर्मुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह सहायक होगी :
questions.text_english: Golden rice is a promising transgenic crop. When released for cultivation, it will help in :

options.A: पेट्रोल के समान ईंधन के उत्पादन में
options.B: मानव में विटामिन A की कमी को कम करने में

options_english.B: Reduction of Vitamin A deficiency in humans

questions.solution: Golden rice is a genetically modified, transgenic crop engineered to be rich in beta-carotene, which is a precursor to Vitamin A. Its cultivation and consumption are specifically intended to help reduce Vitamin A deficiency in human populations.
questions.solution_hindi: गोल्डन राइस एक अनुवांशिक रूप से रूपांतरित फसल है जो बीटा-कैरोटीन (विटामिन ए का पूर्वगामी) से समृद्ध होती है। यह विशेष रूप से मानव आबादी में विटामिन A की कमी को दूर करने में सहायक है।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए आरेखों द्वारा चार विभिन्न अनुलेखन इकाइयों को दर्शाया गया है। उचित प्रकार से अभिचित्रित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Four different transcription units are shown below. Choose the option with the correct image.
questions.solution: In a transcription unit, the promoter is conventionally located towards the 5' end of the coding strand. The terminator is located towards the 3' end of the coding strand. The template strand has 3' to 5' polarity. Option D correctly depicts this arrangement.
questions.solution_hindi: एक अनुलेखन इकाई में, उन्नायक (Promoter) पारंपरिक रूप से कोडिंग रज्जुक के 5' सिरे पर स्थित होता है और समापक (Terminator) 3' सिरे पर होता है। टेम्प्लेट रज्जुक की ध्रुवता 3' से 5' होती है। विकल्प (D) इस व्यवस्था को सही ढंग से दर्शाता है।

questions.text: प्रतिजैविक-प्रतिरोधी जीवाणु का प्रादुर्भाव जिस प्रकार के विकास का उदाहरण है, वह है :
questions.text_english: Appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of evolution due to:
questions.solution: The appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of evolution by anthropogenic action. This occurs because the excessive and indiscriminate use of antibiotics by humans creates a selection pressure that favours the survival and rapid multiplication of resistant bacterial strains.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिजैविक-प्रतिरोधी जीवाणु का प्रादुर्भाव मानवजनित कार्यकलापों द्वारा विकास का एक उदाहरण है। यह मनुष्यों द्वारा एंटीबायोटिक दवाओं के अत्यधिक उपयोग के कारण उत्पन्न चयन दबाव का परिणाम है।

questions.text:
उस कथन को पहचानिए जो डार्विन के विकासवाद का सही ढंग से वर्णन करता है।
(i) जीवों का अतिशय उत्पादन स्पर्धा उत्पन्न करता है।
(ii) विविधता आनुवंशिक (वंशागत) है जो विकास का कारक है।
(iii) उपार्जित लक्षण वंशानुगत होते हैं।
(iv) उत्तरजीविता अनुकूलित विशेषकों (लक्षणों) पर निर्भर करती है।
(v) अनुकूली विविधताओं के संग्रहित होने से नई जाति (स्पीशीज़) का उद्भव होता है।
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Identify the statements that correctly describe Darwin's Theory of Evolution.
(i) Overproduction of organisms leads to competition.
(ii) Variation is inherited and causes evolution.
(iii) Acquired characters are inherited.
(iv) Survival depends on favourable traits.
(v) New species arise due to accumulation of favourable variations.
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection states that populations overproduce, variations are inherited, survival depends on favourable traits, and accumulation of these traits leads to speciation. The inheritance of acquired characters is a concept proposed by Lamarck, not Darwin. Therefore, statements (i), (ii), (iv), and (v) correctly describe Darwin's theory.
questions.solution_hindi: डार्विन के प्राकृतिक वरण के सिद्धांत के अनुसार जीवों का अतिशय उत्पादन स्पर्धा उत्पन्न करता है, विविधता आनुवंशिक होती है, उत्तरजीविता अनुकूलित विशेषकों पर निर्भर करती है और अनुकूली विविधताओं के संग्रहित होने से नई स्पीशीज़ का उद्भव होता है। उपार्जित लक्षणों की वंशागति लैमार्क का सिद्धांत है। अतः कथन (i), (ii), (iv) तथा (v) सही हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ऐस्केरिसता (ऐस्केरिएसिस) का अभिलक्षण नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a symptom of Ascariasis ?
questions.solution: The common symptoms of Ascariasis include internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anaemia, and blockage of the intestinal passage. Skin ulcers are not a symptom of Ascariasis; they are typically associated with other infections or skin conditions.
questions.solution_hindi: ऐस्केरिएसिस के सामान्य लक्षणों में आन्तरिक रक्तस्राव, पेशीय पीड़ा, ज्वर, अरक्तता (एनीमिया) और आंत्र का अवरोध शामिल हैं। त्वचीय व्रण (स्किन अल्सर) ऐस्केरिएसिस का लक्षण नहीं है।

questions.text: एक विशिष्ट समय पर प्रत्येक पोषण स्तर के जीवित पदार्थ की विशिष्ट मात्रा होती है। इसे क्या कहते हैं?
questions.text_english: Every trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time. What is it called?
questions.solution: The mass of living biological material (biomass) present at a particular trophic level at a specific given time is referred to as the standing crop.
questions.solution_hindi: एक विशिष्ट समय पर प्रत्येक पोषण स्तर में मौजूद जीवित जैविक पदार्थ (बायोमास) की मात्रा को स्थित शस्य या खड़ी फ़सल (Standing crop) कहा जाता है।

questions.text: डीएनए अणु का सबसे छोटा भाग जिसे बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन द्वारा बदला जा सकता है, वह है :
questions.text_english: The smallest part of DNA molecule that can be changed by point mutation is :
questions.solution: A point mutation involves a change in a single base pair of DNA. Therefore, the smallest part of the DNA molecule that is altered during a point mutation is a single nucleotide.
questions.solution_hindi: बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन (पॉइंट म्यूटेशन) में डीएनए के एकल क्षार युग्म में परिवर्तन होता है। इसलिए, डीएनए अणु का सबसे छोटा भाग जिसे बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन द्वारा बदला जा सकता है, वह एक न्यूक्लियोटाइड है।

questions.text:
ड्रग तथा ऐल्कोहॉल के विषय में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं :
(i) किशोर मित्रों के दबाव (प्रभाव) में अधिक शीघ्र आ जाते हैं।
(ii) ड्रग की लत के परिणामस्वरूप (कारण) हमारे शरीर में उपस्थित संवेदीग्राहियों के प्रति सहनशीलता अधिक हो जाती है।
(iii) ऐल्कोहॉल केन्द्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है।
(iv) ड्रग के अत्यधिक उपयोग से ऊर्जा शक्ति बढ़ाने में सहायता मिलती है।
(v) उपचयी स्टेरॉइड्स आक्रामकता का अवनमन (कम) करते हैं।
सही कथन/कथनों वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Some statements regarding drugs and alcohol are given below :
(i) Adolescents are more vulnerable to peer pressure.
(ii) Drug addiction leads to increased tolerance level of the receptors present in our body.
(iii) Alcohol affects the central nervous system.
(iv) Excessive use of drugs helps to increase energy.
(v) Anabolic steroids decrease aggressiveness.
Choose the option with correct statement(s).
questions.solution: Adolescents are indeed more vulnerable to peer pressure. Repeated use of drugs increases the tolerance level of receptors, prompting greater consumption. Alcohol acts as a depressant and directly affects the central nervous system. Conversely, anabolic steroids typically increase aggressiveness, and excessive drug use does not universally help increase natural energy. Hence, statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.
questions.solution_hindi: किशोर वास्तव में मित्रों के दबाव के प्रति अधिक सुभेद्य होते हैं। नशीली दवाओं का बार-बार उपयोग ग्राही (रिसेप्टर्स) के सहिष्णुता स्तर को बढ़ाता है, जिससे अधिक सेवन को बढ़ावा मिलता है। ऐल्कोहॉल सीधे केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है। इसके विपरीत, एनाबॉलिक स्टेरॉयड आम तौर पर आक्रामकता बढ़ाते हैं, और नशीली दवाओं का अत्यधिक उपयोग स्वाभाविक रूप से ऊर्जा नहीं बढ़ाता है। अतः कथन (i), (ii) और (iii) सही हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पौधों के उस जोड़े वाले सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिनमें जल द्वारा परागण होता है।
questions.text_english: Select the correct option for the pair of plants pollinated by water.

options.D: वाटर हायसिंथ तथा जल कुमुदिनी (वाटर लिली)

questions.solution: Both Vallisneria and Hydrilla are aquatic plants that rely exclusively on water currents for the transfer of pollen grains, a process known as hydrophily. While Water lily and Water hyacinth are aquatic plants, their flowers emerge above the water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind.
questions.solution_hindi: वैलिसनेरिया और हाइड्रिला दोनों ही ऐसे जलीय पौधे हैं जो परागकणों के स्थानांतरण के लिए पूरी तरह से जलधाराओं पर निर्भर होते हैं (जल परागण)। हालाँकि जल कुमुदिनी (वाटर लिली) और वाटर हायसिंथ जलीय पौधे हैं, लेकिन उनके फूल पानी की सतह से ऊपर निकलते हैं और वे कीड़ों या हवा द्वारा परागित होते हैं।

The allele for brown eyes (B) is dominant over blue eyes (b). In a population, 36% of individuals have blue eyes.
Assuming Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, calculate :
(i) Frequency of allele B
(ii) Percentage of heterozygous individuals
(iii) Percentage of individuals that are homozygous dominant
(Working to be shown)

key_points: Calculate q (recessive allele frequency) from q^2 = 0.36 -> q = 0.6
Calculate p (dominant allele B frequency) -> p = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4
Calculate 2pq for heterozygous percentage -> 2 * 0.4 * 0.6 = 0.48 or 48%
Calculate p^2 for homozygous dominant percentage -> 0.4^2 = 0.16 or 16%

sub_questions.solution: According to the Hardy-Weinberg principle, the frequency of the recessive phenotype (blue eyes) is q^2, which is given as 0.36. Thus, the frequency of the recessive allele 'b' (q) is 0.6, making the frequency of the dominant allele 'B' (p) equal to 0.4. The percentage of heterozygous individuals (2pq) is calculated as 2 multiplied by 0.4 and 0.6, yielding 0.48 or 48%. The percentage of homozygous dominant individuals (p^2) is the square of 0.4, which equals 0.16 or 16%.

questions.text_english: What did Henking observe in his experiments on insects that led to the discovery of sex chromosome? How did his observation contribute to our understanding of sex determination?

key_points: State Henking's observation of the X body in 50% of sperms during spermatogenesis
Explain that this X body was later identified as the X chromosome
Explain that this contributed to the understanding of the XO type of sex determination mechanism in insects

questions.solution: Henking observed a specific nuclear structure that he named the X body, which was present in exactly 50 percent of the sperms during spermatogenesis in certain insects, while the other 50 percent lacked it. This critical observation contributed significantly to our understanding of sex determination by demonstrating that the X body was actually a chromosome, eventually named the X chromosome, and it established the foundation for the XO type of sex determination mechanism where the presence or absence of this specific chromosome determines the sex of the offspring.

key_points: State reason: DNA is transparent or not stained with ethidium bromide

sub_questions.solution: The DNA fragments might not be visible because they are transparent and were likely not stained with the required compound. To make them visible, the gel must be stained with ethidium bromide and subsequently exposed to ultraviolet radiation, which makes the DNA bands appear as bright orange bands. To collect specific DNA fragments for further use, the separated bands are carefully cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece through a purification process known as elution.

questions.solution: The full form of GEAC is the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee. questions.text_english:
Answer the following questions:
(a) Explain the different ways by which apomictic seeds can be developed.
(b) Mention one advantage of apomictic seeds for farmers.

key_points: Explain development from a diploid egg cell formed without reduction division that develops without fertilization
Explain development from nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac that start dividing and protrude into the embryo sac
State advantage: prevents segregation of desirable hybrid traits, eliminating the need to buy new hybrid seeds every year

questions.solution: Apomictic seeds can be developed through several natural mechanisms, such as when a diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and subsequently develops into an embryo without undergoing fertilization. Another common way is when some of the diploid nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac, and directly develop into embryos. The major advantage of apomictic seeds for farmers is that they prevent the segregation of desirable hybrid traits, allowing farmers to continuously sow the seeds year after year to raise the same hybrid crop without having to buy new, expensive hybrid seeds each season.

questions.text_english:
(a) What is meant by translation in protein synthesis?
(b) Explain charging of tRNA (aminoacylation of tRNA) and mention its importance in the process of translation.

key_points: Define translation as the process of polymerizing amino acids to form a polypeptide based on the sequence of codons in mRNA
Explain charging of tRNA as the process where specific amino acids are linked to their corresponding tRNAs in the presence of ATP
State importance: provides the necessary energetic bond between the amino acid and tRNA required for the formation of peptide bonds

questions.solution: Translation in protein synthesis refers to the highly coordinated biological process where the sequence of codons present on a messenger RNA molecule is decoded to polymerize amino acids and form a specific polypeptide chain. Charging of tRNA, also known as aminoacylation of tRNA, is the preparatory phase where specific amino acids are enzymatically linked to their corresponding tRNA molecules in the presence of ATP. This step is critically important for the translation process because the energetic bond formed between the amino acid and the tRNA provides the necessary energy for the subsequent formation of peptide bonds between adjacent amino acids on the ribosome.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रोटीन संश्लेषण में स्थानांतरण (अनुवादन) उस जैविक प्रक्रिया को कहते हैं जिसमें मैसेंजर आरएनए पर मौजूद प्रकूटों (कोडॉन) के अनुक्रम को डिकोड करके अमीनो अम्लों को बहुलकीकृत किया जाता है और एक विशिष्ट पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला बनाई जाती है। अंतरण आरएनए के आवेशीकरण (ऐमीनोऐसिलेशन) वह प्रारंभिक चरण है जिसमें ATP की उपस्थिति में विशिष्ट अमीनो अम्ल अपने संबंधित tRNA अणुओं से एंजाइमी रूप से जुड़ जाते हैं। यह कदम इसलिए महत्त्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि अमीनो अम्ल और tRNA के बीच बनने वाला ऊर्जावान बंधन राइबोसोम पर आसन्न अमीनो अम्लों के बीच पेप्टाइड बांड के निर्माण के लिए आवश्यक ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है।

(ख) उस वृद्धि वक्र की व्याख्या कीजिए जिसमें इस क्षमता का ध्यान रखा जाता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) What is the carrying capacity of a species in a habitat?
(b) Explain the growth curve that takes this capacity into account.

key_points: Define carrying capacity as the maximum population size that a habitat's resources can sustain indefinitely
Identify the growth curve as the logistic growth curve
Explain the phases: lag phase, phase of acceleration, phase of deceleration, and asymptote when population density balances with carrying capacity (forming a sigmoid curve)

questions.solution: The carrying capacity of a habitat represents the maximum population size of a specific biological species that the environment can indefinitely sustain, given the available resources such as food, water, and habitat space, beyond which no further population growth is possible. The growth curve that takes this biological capacity into account is the logistic growth curve. In this model, a population initially experiences a lag phase, followed by a phase of rapid acceleration and deceleration, and eventually reaches an asymptote when the population density perfectly balances out with the habitat's carrying capacity, resulting in a sigmoid or S-shaped curve.
questions.solution_hindi: किसी आवास की पोषण क्षमता (carrying capacity) उस अधिकतम जनसंख्या आकार को दर्शाती है जिसे वह पर्यावरण अनिश्चित काल तक बनाए रख सकता है, जो उपलब्ध संसाधनों जैसे भोजन और स्थान पर निर्भर करता है, और जिसके आगे जनसंख्या में और वृद्धि संभव नहीं है। वह वृद्धि वक्र जो इस क्षमता का ध्यान रखता है, लॉजिस्टिक वृद्धि वक्र कहलाता है। इस मॉडल में, जनसंख्या शुरू में एक लैग चरण (lag phase) का अनुभव करती है, उसके बाद तीव्र त्वरण और मंदी का चरण आता है, और अंततः जब जनसंख्या घनत्व आवास की पोषण क्षमता के साथ संतुलित हो जाता है, तो यह एक अनंतस्पर्शी (asymptote) तक पहुँच जाता है, जिससे एक सिग्मॉइड या एस-आकार का वक्र बनता है।

questions.text_english:
In vitro fertilization (IVF) is a popular method these days that is helping childless couples to bear a child.
(a) Write the different steps that are carried out in this technique.
(b) Would you consider gamete intra fallopian transfer as a type of IVF? Justify your answer.

key_points: State steps of IVF: hormonal stimulation, retrieval of ova and sperm, fertilization in a lab dish under simulated conditions, and embryo transfer (ZIFT or IUT) to the female
State that Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) is not a type of IVF
Justify that in GIFT, fertilization occurs naturally inside the female's body (in vivo), not externally in a lab dish

questions.solution: In vitro fertilization encompasses several meticulous steps starting with the controlled stimulation of the ovaries to produce multiple ova, followed by their surgical retrieval. These harvested ova are then combined with sperm in a sterile laboratory dish under highly simulated conditions to facilitate successful fertilization. Following a brief incubation period, the resulting early embryos or zygotes are carefully transferred directly into the female's uterus or fallopian tube to establish a pregnancy. Gamete intra fallopian transfer is generally not considered a strict type of IVF because fertilization occurs naturally inside the female's reproductive tract (in vivo) rather than externally in a laboratory dish, even though the gametes themselves are medically handled and transferred.
questions.solution_hindi: इन विट्रो फर्टिलाइजेशन (IVF) में कई चरण शामिल हैं: सबसे पहले अंडाशय को उत्तेजित कर कई अंडे उत्पन्न किए जाते हैं, जिन्हें बाद में शल्य चिकित्सा द्वारा निकाल लिया जाता है। इसके बाद प्रयोगशाला में नियंत्रित स्थितियों के तहत इन अंडों को शुक्राणु के साथ मिलाकर निषेचन कराया जाता है। इसके बाद विकसित हो रहे भ्रूण या युग्मनज (जाइगोट) को महिला के गर्भाशय या फैलोपियन ट्यूब में स्थानांतरित कर दिया जाता है ताकि गर्भावस्था स्थापित हो सके। युग्मक अंतराफैलोपी स्थानांतरण (GIFT) को IVF का प्रकार नहीं माना जाता है क्योंकि इसमें निषेचन प्रयोगशाला में (इन विट्रो) न होकर प्राकृतिक रूप से महिला के शरीर के अंदर (इन विवो) होता है।

questions.text_english: Draw a neat diagram of a maize grain showing the internal structure and label any five parts.

key_points: Draw the longitudinal section of a maize grain
Label fused pericarp and seed coat
Label starchy endosperm
Label proteinaceous aleurone layer
Label single cotyledon (scutellum)
Label coleoptile and plumule
Label coleorhiza and radicle

questions.solution: Draw a neat diagram showing the longitudinal section of a maize grain. The important parts to be clearly labelled include the outermost fused pericarp and seed coat. The large starchy endosperm should be demarcated from the embryo by the proteinaceous aleurone layer. Within the embryo region, the single large cotyledon known as the scutellum must be depicted. Furthermore, the embryonic shoot axis containing the plumule and its protective sheath, the coleoptile, along with the embryonic root axis containing the radicle and its protective sheath, the coleorhiza, must be accurately identified and labelled.
questions.solution_hindi: मक्का के दाने का अनुदैर्ध्य काट (longitudinal section) दर्शाता हुआ एक स्वच्छ आरेख बनाएं। इसमें सबसे बाहरी परत के रूप में बीजावरण और फलभित्ति (pericarp) को नामांकित करें। भ्रूण और बड़े स्टार्चयुक्त भ्रूणपोष (endosperm) को अलग करने वाली प्रोटीनयुक्त परत, एल्यूरोन परत को दर्शाएं। भ्रूण के हिस्से में एकल बड़े बीजपत्र (scutellum) को नामांकित करें। इसके साथ ही प्रांकुर (plumule) और उसके आवरण प्रांकुरचोल (coleoptile), तथा मूलांकुर (radicle) और उसके आवरण मूलांकुरचोल (coleorhiza) को भी स्पष्ट रूप से नामांकित करें।

questions.text_english:
Cow dung and water are mixed and fed into a biogas plant to allow digestion of biowastes. The person performing this process says that there is no need to provide an inoculum.
(a) Do you agree with him? Justify your answer.
(b) What happens to the biowaste inside the digester ?
(c) Name the useful by-products obtained from this process and mention how they are used.

key_points: State agreement with the person
Justify that cow dung naturally contains abundant methanogenic bacteria required for anaerobic breakdown
Explain that inside the digester, anaerobic methanogens break down complex organic biowaste into simpler compounds without oxygen
Name by-products: Biogas (methane, CO2) used as fuel for cooking/lighting, and spent slurry used as nutrient-rich organic fertilizer

questions.solution: I agree with the person performing the process because cow dung naturally contains a rich and abundant population of methanogenic bacteria, including Methanobacterium, which are essential for anaerobic breakdown. Therefore, adding an external biological inoculum is not strictly necessary. Inside the digester tank, the complex organic biowaste from the dung is systematically broken down by these anaerobic methanogens under strictly oxygen-free conditions into simpler compounds. The highly useful by-products obtained from this complete process are biogas, which is primarily a mixture of methane and carbon dioxide used universally as a renewable fuel for cooking and lighting, and the spent slurry, which is subsequently removed and extensively utilised as an excellent nutrient-rich organic fertilizer for agricultural crops.

questions.solution: T.H. Morgan conducted extensive dihybrid cross experiments on Drosophila melanogaster to deeply study genes that were sex-linked. He crossed yellow-bodied, white-eyed females with wild-type brown-bodied, red-eyed males and subsequently intercrossed their F1 progeny to closely observe the segregation of these two specific traits across generations. The observed results deviated significantly from the classic Mendelian inheritance pattern because the two genes did not assort independently; the F2 generation ratio was completely different from the expected 9:3:3:1 ratio due to the physical association of the genes on the same X chromosome. To specifically describe these observations, Morgan coined the term linkage to denote the physical association of genes on a chromosome, and the term recombination to accurately describe the generation of non-parental gene combinations due to crossing over.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Describe the series of experiments conducted by Frederick Griffith. Comment on the significance of the result obtained.
(ii) State the contribution of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty.

key_points: Describe Griffith's experiments using S and R strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae on mice
Detail the four cases: live S -> mice die, live R -> mice live, heat-killed S -> mice live, heat-killed S + live R -> mice die
Explain significance: discovery of the transforming principle enabling R strain to become virulent
State contribution of Avery, MacLeod, McCarty: biochemical characterization showing that DNA is the genetic material responsible for transformation

sub_questions.solution: Frederick Griffith conducted a series of elegant experiments using Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteria and laboratory mice. He worked with two distinct bacterial strains: a smooth (S) strain that possessed a protective polysaccharide capsule and was highly virulent, and a rough (R) strain that lacked the capsule and was non-virulent. When he injected living S strain bacteria, the mice tragically died of pneumonia, whereas those injected with the R strain easily survived. Surprisingly, when he injected heat-killed S strain bacteria, the mice survived, proving the heat destroyed the bacteria's lethal capability. However, the critical breakthrough occurred when he injected a mixture of heat-killed S strain and living R strain bacteria; the mice contracted pneumonia and died, and living S strain bacteria were successfully recovered from their bodies. The immense significance of these profound results was Griffith's conclusion that the living R strain bacteria had somehow been genetically transformed by a mysterious "transforming principle" transferred directly from the heat-killed S strain, enabling them to synthesize a smooth capsule and become virulent. This laid the initial foundation for identifying the genetic material. Subsequently, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty made a monumental contribution by biochemically isolating and purifying DNA, RNA, and proteins from the heat-killed S cells. By systematically using specific degrading enzymes like proteases, RNases, and DNases, they conclusively proved that only the digestion of DNA completely halted the transformation process. This provided the first definitive biochemical evidence that DNA, and not protein or RNA, was the actual genetic material responsible for inheriting traits.

The following questions are based on haemophilia.
(i) Work out the crosses between :
(I) Normal female and Haemophilic male
(II) Carrier female and Normal male
(III) Carrier female and Haemophilic male
(ii) Write the conclusions you draw from these crosses. Comment on the type of inheritance of the disease.
(Use: X - Normal, Xh - Haemophilic)

key_points: Perform cross I: XX × XhY -> daughters are carriers (XXh), sons are normal (XY)
Perform cross II: XXh × XY -> 50% sons haemophilic (XhY), 50% daughters carriers (XXh), others normal
Perform cross III: XXh × XhY -> 50% daughters haemophilic, 50% carriers; 50% sons haemophilic, 50% normal
Conclude that males are affected if mother is a carrier, while females are affected only if father is haemophilic and mother is a carrier
State that the disease follows an X-linked recessive type of inheritance

sub_questions.solution: To analyse the inheritance of haemophilia, we meticulously evaluate the three specific genetic crosses using X for the normal allele and Xh for the recessive haemophilic allele. In the first cross between a completely normal female (XX) and a haemophilic male (XhY), all the resulting female offspring receive the affected Xh chromosome from the father, becoming asymptomatic genetic carriers (XXh), while all the male offspring receive the normal X chromosome from the mother, remaining completely healthy (XY). In the second cross between a carrier female (XXh) and a normal male (XY), there is a fifty percent probability that a male child will be born haemophilic (XhY) by inheriting the affected allele from the mother, while the female children will either be completely normal or asymptomatic carriers. In the third cross between a carrier female (XXh) and a haemophilic male (XhY), the offspring face severe outcomes: half the females will be tragically haemophilic (XhXh) and half will be carriers, whereas half the males will be affected (XhY) and half will be normal. From these detailed crosses, we draw the firm conclusion that the disease is transmitted predominantly from carrier mothers to their male offspring, and females are only affected if the father is affected and the mother is at least a carrier. This comprehensive pattern categorically confirms that haemophilia follows an X-linked recessive type of inheritance, where the defective gene is securely located on the X chromosome and its expression is masked by a normal dominant allele in heterozygous females.

(i) Explain any two basic principles/core techniques on which biotechnology is based.

key_points: Explain genetic engineering: altering the chemistry of genetic material and introducing it into hosts

sub_questions.solution: The rapid advancement of modern biotechnology is fundamentally anchored on two core principles. The first is genetic engineering, which involves highly specialized techniques aimed at deliberately altering the precise chemistry of genetic material, encompassing both DNA and RNA. This altered genetic material is subsequently introduced into a host organism, completely modifying the host's fundamental phenotypic characteristics. The second critical principle is bioprocess engineering, which strictly mandates the meticulous maintenance of completely sterile and contamination-free conditions within large-scale biochemical manufacturing processes. This rigorous sterility ensures the exclusive growth and unhindered multiplication of only the specifically desired microbe or genetically engineered eukaryotic cell in massive quantities, facilitating the successful industrial production of invaluable biotechnological products like life-saving antibiotics, therapeutic vaccines, and specialized enzymes. To successfully execute recombinant DNA technology, three exceptionally key tools are universally utilized. First, restriction endonucleases are indispensable enzymes acting as precise molecular scissors; they identify specific palindromic recognition sequences on the DNA and selectively cut the sugar-phosphate backbone, producing specific fragments required for gene manipulation. Second, cloning vectors, typically resilient plasmids or bacteriophages, act as highly efficient molecular delivery vehicles; they are explicitly used to carry the isolated foreign DNA fragment and safely transfer it directly into the selected host cell, ensuring it replicates flawlessly along with the host genome. Third, a competent host organism, usually a treated bacterial cell, is absolutely required to physically receive, harbor, and continuously replicate the newly formed recombinant DNA molecule, enabling the mass cloning and ultimate expression of the inserted foreign gene.

"Early and accurate diagnosis of diseases is vital in medical technology."
(i) Name the conventional methods of diagnosis and their disadvantages.
(ii) Which three diagnostic techniques have been developed through Biotechnology ? Explain how each one helps in detecting diseases.

key_points: Name conventional methods: Serum and urine analysis
State disadvantages: Cannot detect pathogens reliably at low concentrations during early stages
Name and explain PCR: Amplifies minute DNA/RNA amounts to detect pathogens or mutations early
Name and explain ELISA: Detects pathogenic antigens or the specific antibodies synthesized against them
Name and explain Recombinant DNA with Autoradiography: Uses a radioactive probe to hybridize with normal genes; mutated genes fail to appear on film

sub_questions.solution: Early and accurate diagnosis of diseases is exceptionally vital in medical technology because it directly enables the prompt initiation of targeted therapeutic interventions, vastly improving patient survival rates. The most universally utilized conventional methods of diagnosis heavily rely on routine serum and urine analysis. However, a major disadvantage of these traditional methods is their inherent lack of extreme sensitivity; they completely fail to reliably detect the presence of highly dangerous pathogens during the crucial early stages of an infection when the concentration of the bacteria or virus in the body is still incredibly low. To overcome these severe limitations, modern biotechnology has successfully developed highly advanced diagnostic techniques. The first is the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), which is remarkably helpful because it can exponentially amplify minute and almost undetectable fragments of pathogenic DNA or RNA, allowing clinicians to definitively confirm the presence of deadly viruses like HIV or crucial genetic mutations in suspected cancer patients even when symptoms are entirely absent. The second technique is the Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA), which functions on the highly specific principle of antigen-antibody interaction; it provides immense diagnostic assistance by swiftly and accurately detecting the physical presence of specific pathogenic antigens in a patient's blood sample or by identifying the specialized antibodies the patient's immune system has newly synthesized against the invading pathogen. The third revolutionary technique involves Recombinant DNA technology combined with precise Autoradiography. In this method, a specially designed, radioactively tagged single-stranded DNA or RNA probe is allowed to hybridize with its complementary sequence in a clone of cells. Upon subsequent exposure to photographic film, mutated genes completely fail to appear on the autoradiogram because the highly specific probe cannot successfully bind to the mutated sequence, powerfully assisting doctors in conclusively identifying life-threatening genetic disorders.

(i) Trace the development of a gamete mother cell till its release from the ovary during ovulation.
(ii) Name the two pituitary hormones that play an important role in the process.

key_points: Trace path: Oogonia -> Primary oocyte (arrested in prophase I) -> Primary follicle -> Secondary follicle -> Tertiary follicle -> completion of meiosis I -> Secondary oocyte and first polar body -> Graafian follicle -> Ovulation
Name hormones: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH)

sub_questions.solution: Oogenesis is a highly complex and discontinuous biological process detailing the formation of a mature female gamete. The process strictly begins before birth during embryonic development when millions of specialized gamete mother cells, called oogonia, are massively generated within the fetal ovary. These oogonia subsequently enter the crucial prophase-I stage of the first meiotic division but become temporarily arrested in this specific state, and are now officially termed primary oocytes. Each primary oocyte becomes enveloped by a single layer of granulosa cells, forming a primary follicle. A massive degeneration of these follicles occurs prior to puberty. Following the onset of puberty, hormonal triggers stimulate the primary follicle to systematically mature into a secondary and then a tertiary follicle. Within the mature tertiary follicle, the primary oocyte finally completes its long-arrested first meiotic division, resulting in a highly unequal cellular division that yields a massive, nutrient-rich secondary oocyte and a tiny, non-functional first polar body. The tertiary follicle then fully matures into the specialized Graafian follicle. Ultimately, the Graafian follicle ruptures under hormonal influence, violently releasing the secondary oocyte from the ovary in a critical event universally known as ovulation. The two indispensable pituitary hormones that play incredibly important roles in actively regulating this entire process are Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), which drives the initial growth and maturation of the ovarian follicles, and Luteinizing Hormone (LH), which triggers the final pivotal surge that induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle and causes ovulation.

key_points: Draw diagram of a pollen grain labeling vegetative and generative cells

sub_questions.solution: A neatly drawn and correctly labelled diagram of the two-celled stage of the male gametophyte of an angiosperm (pollen grain) must clearly display the large, irregularly shaped vegetative cell occupying the bulk of the interior and the distinct, spindle-shaped generative cell floating freely within the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. Starting strictly from the innermost boundary and proceeding outward, the three protective layers that securely surround the dense cytoplasm of the male gametophyte are the delicate plasma membrane, followed by the thin and continuous inner wall called the intine, and finally, the thick, highly sculpted outer layer known as the exine. The outermost layer, the exine, is structurally composed of a remarkable organic material known as sporopollenin. The profound biological advantage of sporopollenin is that it is one of the most highly resistant organic materials known to science; it can effortlessly withstand extreme high temperatures and highly destructive strong acids or alkalis, while remaining completely impervious to degradation by any known enzymes, thereby providing immense evolutionary protection to the fragile pollen grain during harsh environmental exposure. However, the exine layer of the male gametophyte is deliberately not continuous; it inherently possesses prominent, specialized apertures specifically called germ pores, which are critical regions entirely devoid of sporopollenin. These specific unfortified regions are absolutely essential because they provide a necessary structural exit point, effortlessly allowing the vital pollen tube to successfully emerge during the crucial process of pollen germination on the stigma.
